editorial.dek: A spot-check thermometer: pull it, press it, read it, put it back in the drawer.
editorial.best_for: Checking doneness without committing to a cook
editorial.catch: It tells you where the food is at the moment you ask. Nothing is watching it while you are doing something else.
check_before_buying: Confirm the accuracy figure on the live listing before you build a plan around ±0.5°F.
Note what the reading is measuring: a thermometer is only as good as the spot you put it in.
If you are cooking for hours, compare it against a leave-in probe before you rely on a single spot check.

blocking_questions.question: Did the five people-supplied links mean these five products, or were they placeholders?
blocking_questions.answer: No — the supplied tokens do not identify products, and they were never meant to. Each token is 9 characters; an ASIN is a 10-character code, so a token cannot be one. The mapping in this register is what the links resolve to, recorded live on five separate occasions, four of which reproduced the mapping exactly (5/5 each time). The fifth, on 2026-11-20, saw one token land on the Amazon homepage instead of its recorded listing — logged as FLG-030, which neither confirms nor invalidates the mapping. Nothing public binds the short code to a product, so the intended fields stay blank and the observed target is kept in its own column. The intended fields are settled as “unknown”, which is a settled answer, not a gap in the record.

blocking_questions.question: Which of the observed spec conflicts are real: B08DKYBTPH model and max temperature, ThermoMaven canonical ASIN, Emeril accessory count?
blocking_questions.answer: The conflicts are real in the listings; which side is right needs the manufacturer. All five listing pages were re-read on 2026-11-20. The Chefman 8 Qt title still reads “TurboFry® 4-in-1 with 450°F Hi-Fry” while the captured copy says 200–400°F; the Emeril title still says “Six Cooking Accessories Included”; the ThermoMaven title wording rotated again. A listing can contradict itself without either side being wrong, so the honest record is the conflict, not a chosen value. This site publishes the listing's own wording and flags the conflict.

redirect_observation.note: Observed target is B0DHZTCNR5, not the B0DMDQZTZN variant URL — this reduces but does not close FLG-004, because the redirect carries a fallback flag rather than a canonical resolution.

faq: The listing states a tolerance of +/-0.5F, names NIST and NSF certification, and describes an auto-rotating LED screen and IP67 waterproofing. Those are the listing's claims; nobody on this desk has tested the device, so no measured figure appears anywhere on this site.

It is not shown on the US listing's product-details table in the read of 2026-11-20. An 'HT07' model string appears on the brand's French listing, which is why the specs table marks the model unconfirmed for the US page instead of asserting it (FLG-004).
Does it work in an air fryer?

It is an instant-read device: you put the tip in the food for a second and read the number off the device. For a probe that stays in the food while it cooks, the other thermometer in this shop is the one whose listing names air-fryer use.
